problem: The horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{7{x}^{3}+2x-5}{{x}^{2}(2{x}^{2}+3)}$ is $y=${{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The given function can be rewritten as follows:

$$
f(x)=\frac{7{x}^{3}+2x-5}{2{x}^{4}+3{x}^{2}}
$$

To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{4}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{4},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{7{x}^{3}+2x-5}{2{x}^{4}+3{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{7{x}^{3}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{2x}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{5}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{7}{x}+\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{5}{{x}^{4}})}{(2+\frac{3}{{x}^{2}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{7}{x},$ $\frac{2}{{x}^{3}},$ $\frac{5}{{x}^{4}},$ and $\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{7}{x}+\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{5}{{x}^{4}})}{(2+\frac{3}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & \to \frac{0+0-0}{2+0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=0.$
